Population of legislative districts by Region, Province, and selected Highly Urbanized/Component City : 2020 |publisher=[[Philippine Statistics Authority]] |accessdate=June 17, 2022}} |electorate = 81,404 (2025){{cite web |title=Data on the Total Number Established and Clustered Precincts, Registered Voters and Voting Centers |url=https://comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2025NLE/Statistics/CONSOLIDATED_2025_Number_Of_Registered_Voters.pdf |website=Commission on Elections|accessdate=July 21, 2025}} |area = {{convert|337.49|sqkm|sqmi|abbr=on}} |towns = |year = 1984 |members_label = Representative |members = [[Zaldy Villa]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Partido Federal ng Pilipinas}}|border=darkgray}} [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas|PFP]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = TBD }} '''Siquijor's at-large congressional district''' is the provincewide [[congressional district of the Philippines|electoral district]] in [[Siquijor]], Philippines. The province has been represented in the country's [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|national legislatures]] since 1984.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 16, 2021}} It first elected a representative [[at-large]] during the [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election]] following the restoration of provincial and city district representation in the [[Batasang Pambansa]] where Siquijor had previously been included in the regionwide representation of [[Central Visayas]] (Region VII) for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa|interim parliament]].{{cite web|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l82d3 |title=Batas Pambansa Blg. 660, (1984-03-07) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=March 16, 2021}} The province, created by the 1971 separation of [[Siquijor Island]] from [[Negros Oriental]], was formerly represented as part of [[Negros Oriental's 2nd congressional district|that province's 2nd district]] in earlier legislatures.{{cite web|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l564a |title=Republic Act No. 6398, (1971-09-17) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=March 16, 2021}} Since the 1987 restoration of Congress following the ratification of a new constitution, Siquijor has been entitled to one member in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=March 16, 2021}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Zaldy Villa]] of the [[Partido Federal ng Pilipinas]] (PFP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=November 9, 2023}}{{cite news|url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1856981/senior-deputy-speaker-gonzales-3-other-lawmakers-join-lakas-cmd-party|title=Senior Deputy Speaker Gonzales, 3 other lawmakers join Lakas-CMD
